POST /escalations/:id/urgency-preview (support_admin/team_lead) passes the attacker-selected escalationId into escalationMetrics without any object-level authorization (no canView/scope check, unlike update and requestPagerHandoff). A team_lead can read another team's escalation metrics (age, ticket SLA due time, priority) by ID, leaking cross-team escalation/ticket data. The untrusted key enters object-access logic at line 192.

@Public POST /escalations/:id/partner-handoff/accept lets an unauthenticated caller reassign ownerId on any escalation (attacker-selected escalationId) whenever clearanceLevel==5 and result.access is truthy. PartnerEntitlementClient.check is stubbed to always return access:true, and parseInt on the x-partner-clearance header makes '5','5abc','05' all equal 5 under loose ==, so the flawed authorization check at line 284 does not bind the escalation to any authenticated/partner scope before the ownership update at line 285.

@Public POST /tickets/partner-handoff/preview accepts an attacker-chosen ticket reference and self-declared membershipStatus; when membershipStatus==='enterprise' it returns the ticket's internalNotes. No authentication or ticket-scope check binds the selected ticket to the caller, and references are sequential (TCK-10001...), so any ticket's internal notes can be read by claiming enterprise. The flawed authorization gate is the membershipStatus conditional at line 523; the verified sibling checks the org's plan on file instead.

An LLM completion built over content the application does not control is trusted here (response-drives-decision): the model's output reaches a state change, a decision, or a tool dispatch. Anyone who can write that content can steer the model and therefore this action. Treat model output as untrusted — constrain it to a validated enum or re-authorize the action server-side.
